author: reek
body: On a machine with no PS/2 controller -- which is most machines made in the last decade -- the firmware's keyboard emulation dies at ExitBootServices and the boot payload goes deaf. The keys are still there, arriving as 8-byte reports on an interrupt endpoint of a USB keyboard. This chapter turns those reports into the same Set-1 scancodes the PS/2 ISR produces, so every consumer above it -- kb-process-scancode, the wizard's text field, the boot menu -- is unchanged and cannot tell the difference.

author: reek
body: The order matters. Modifier presses come before key presses, so Shift is down before H arrives; key releases come before modifier releases, so H lifts before Shift does. A consumer tracking shift state with kb-process-scancode therefore sees exactly the sequence a PS/2 keyboard would have sent.

author: reek
body: F1 through F10 are contiguous at 59; F11 and F12 are not.

author: reek
body: A usage of 0 is an empty slot and 1 is ErrorRollOver; both are below the first real key (4), so "greater than 3" is the liveness test.

author: reek
body: Each of these returns the first difference of its kind, or -1.

author: reek
body: Each applier mutates prev and returns the scancode it implies, or -1 for a change that was applied but names no Set-1 code. Returning -1 rather than 0 keeps "nothing left to do" distinct from "nothing to say about this key".

author: reek
body: A press with no free slot cannot be recorded, so it must not be reported either: prev would never converge and the key would repeat forever. Six down is the report's own limit, so this is unreachable from a conforming device.

author: reek
body: An unmapped change is consumed and the search continues, so a key this table does not name costs one iteration rather than stalling the stream. The fuel bounds that search at more changes than a report can possibly carry (eight modifiers plus six keys, pressed and released).

author: reek
body: The one entry point. Returns the next Set-1 scancode implied by the difference between the last report and this one, or 0 when there is nothing left. An ErrorRollOver report is discarded whole, leaving prev untouched, so the keys still held are not spuriously released.
